title: McCormick envelopes in mixed-integer PDE-constrained optimization
contribution: Carries McCormick relaxations and optimization-based bound tightening into function space for a bilinear, TV-regularized MIPDECO class: cell-averaged relaxations with finitely many inequalities, a priori lower-bound estimates in the mesh size, Gamma-convergence to the pointwise envelope, OBBT validity, and 1D/2D computations (read in arXiv v5).
problem_entry: Missing tool: McCormick relaxations are standard in MINLP B&B but unused in PDE-constrained optimization because the pointwise form gives infinitely many state constraints and OBBT becomes intractable (abstract p. 1; pp. 2, 8).
key_idea: Average the nonlinearity first, uw -> (P_h u)(P_h w), so there are four McCormick inequalities per cell of a coarse partition, then also discretize w with a grid-consistent TV_h (McCh, McChh, pp. 8-11; Fig. 1 p. 8); run OBBT on per-cell bounds (Alg. 1 p. 16).
assumptions: Elliptic A boundedly invertible, compact embedding U into L2, j Lipschitz on bounded sets, C convex bounded closed, BV controls (p. 5); a priori state bounds called 'quite strong' (p. 6); unique solvability of the averaged PDE and valid cell bounds (Assumption 2.7, p. 9); TV_h consistency and Gamma-convergence conditions (pp. 11-13); regularity chosen for cleaner presentation (p. 6).
proof_devices: direct method of the calculus of variations for existence (Prop. 2.5, p. 7)
Lemma A.1: pointwise inequality passes to strong/weak L1 limits, by Egorov's theorem (pp. 33-34)
true minimizer plugged into the approximate relaxation as a feasible point, error charged to a Lipschitz constant times ||u - u_h|| (Thm. 2.8, pp. 9-10)
h^(1/2) control-averaging error via ||w - P_h w||_L1 <= h TV(w) (Thm. 2.11, pp. 11-12)
Gamma-convergence liminf/limsup argument; TV(P_h f) <= TV(f) in 1D (Prop. 2.14, Lemma 2.15, pp. 13-14)
OBBT preserves the assumption behind the error bound, so the bounds increase monotonically (Lemmas 2.16-2.17, Thms. 2.18-2.19, pp. 15-16)
Aubin-Nitsche duality with Galerkin-type orthogonality of cell averaging gives h^2 (Lemma 3.1, pp. 19-21)
explicit sharp embedding constants (Poincare pi^2, Sobolev 4) to certify all assumptions on the example (pp. 17-19)
Lipschitz and Frechet differentiability of the control-to-state map to verify SLIP assumptions (pp. 22-24)
experiments: 1D elliptic example (2048 P1 elements): upper bounds by L-BFGS-B (Huber-smoothed TV) and SLIP; Gurobi lower bounds including an a-posteriori 'tightest' McC using monotonicity bounds (Table 1 p. 27); OBBT time 8.2 s to 1.08e4 s vs 2.14e4 s pointwise (Table 3 p. 29); a priori constant given as a conservative-to-tight range, certified bound beats 0 only on fine meshes (Tables 2, 4, pp. 28-29); OBBT safeguard of 1e-7 (p. 26). 2D convection-diffusion on 48x48 with 8 parallel OBBT rounds: 127 s vs 95,522 s and 400,780 s for similar bounds (pp. 30-32).
positioning: Extends finite-dimensional McCormick and its ODE generalizations (Scott, Barton, Chachuat, Houska) to PDEs; separated from Buchheim et al.'s linear-PDE d=1 bounds; uses the OBBT literature (Gleixner et al.) for cost claims; ties itself to the authors' SLIP line (pp. 2, 6, 14, 22).
writing: Self-described 'recipe' (p. 3); contribution section and roadmap figure (pp. 3, 8); first-person defence of restrictions (p. 3); the abstract already promises gaps, which the conclusion quantifies (pp. 1, 32); remarks on practicality after the theorems; a self-referencing slip in the proof of Thm. 2.19 (p. 16).
limits_future: A priori bound beats trivial bounds only on fine meshes; needs higher-order ||u-u_h|| estimates and a better L_u (p. 32); L-infinity state bounds may be unavailable in several dimensions (p. 33); no 2D a priori analysis (p. 29); future: a posteriori estimates, function-space B&B with adaptive refinement, generalized McCormick for other nonlinearities (pp. 32-33).

transferable: Aggregate a nonlinearity over a coarse partition before relaxing it, so that constraints and bound-tightening subproblems scale with the cells, not the nodes (pp. 8-9).
Approximate-relaxation lower bound = relaxed optimum minus Lipschitz constant times discretization error, proved by plugging the true minimizer into the approximation (pp. 9-10).
Use the Galerkin-type orthogonality of local averaging in a duality argument to gain an extra power of h (pp. 19-21).
OBBT soundness: show that shrinking the feasible set preserves the assumption behind the error bound (pp. 15-16); relax each computed bound by a small safety tolerance (pp. 26, 31).
Report a priori constants as a conservative-to-tight range and show at which mesh sizes the certified bound beats the trivial bound (pp. 28-29).

quotes.text: Consequently, this article will be read as a recipe to first obtain a pointwise generalization of underestimators for nonconvexities as are known from finite-dimensional nonconvex optimization and then approximate this pointwise generalization with finitely many linear inequalities using approximation properties that are due to the PDE setting.
the a priori approximation quality of the lower bound only improves over trivial bounds when the mesh size is already quite fine and the involved constants can be estimated well.

title: A unified funnel restoration SQP algorithm
contribution: Restates funnel globalization as a filter with a single entry inside Uno's four-ingredient double-loop framework, gives trust-region and (first) line-search restoration funnel SQP methods, proves global convergence of the trust-region version by transferring filter-SQP lemmas, and shows on 278 CUTEst problems that the funnel slightly beats Uno's filter on constraint evaluations (read in arXiv v1).
problem_entry: A framework claim (NCO solvers = four ingredients in a double loop) plus a method gap: funnels existed only for equality constraints, as an interior-point trust funnel, or as a tolerance tube without convergence analysis (pp. 2, 4).
key_idea: A funnel is a filter of capacity one whose hmax bound is updated on h-type steps (p. 11); with the switching condition, Armijo on f-type steps and the funnel update tau <- (1-kappa)h + kappa*tau (pp. 8-9), and an always-feasible elastic l1 restoration QP (p. 7), the filter proofs and implementation can be reused (p. 2).
assumptions: Compact iterate set, C2 functions, bounded Hessians (Assumption 1, p. 12); MFCQ for KKT (pp. 3-4); convergence to infeasible points not analysed (p. 7); global QP solution or a Cauchy-point substitute (Remark 1, p. 17); line-search global convergence not proved (p. 15).
proof_devices: feasibility by a case split: infinitely many h-type steps give geometric funnel contraction theta = 1-(1-beta)(1-kappa); finitely many give a telescoping sum of the switching condition against f bounded below (Thm. 1, p. 14)
lemmas transferred from the filter-SQP convergence paper [14], one with an adjusted proof (Lemmas 1, 2, 4, pp. 15-16)
trust-region radius bound for funnel acceptability, Delta^2 <= 2*beta*tau/(mnM) (Lemma 3, p. 15)
finite termination of the inner loop by a case split on h^(k) > 0 vs h^(k) = 0 (Lemma 5, pp. 16-17)
radius-window contradiction: the f-type interval's upper end exceeds twice its lower end, so the inner loop finds a radius inside it (Thm. 2, pp. 17-18)
experiments: Uno on 278 small constrained CUTEst instances, funnel vs filter x trust region vs line search; same initial parameters and QP solver BQPD; kappa=0.5 picked as working well; performance profiles on constraint evaluations, scatter plots, step-type bars for the 49 diverging instances; convexification checked as the cause of line-search underperformance; powellbs and Maratos case studies; public logs; per-instance appendices (pp. 18-24, 27-37).
positioning: Funnel examined 'through the lens of filter methods'; Gould-Toint, Curtis et al., Samadi and a 1995 Dundee tolerance-tube thesis credited; Fletcher-Leyffer-Toint and Wachter-Biegler filter proofs used as the baseline; rivals restated, not criticized (pp. 2-3, 9).
writing: Numbered contributions (i)-(iv) with one 'to our knowledge' priority claim (p. 3); a modest 'slightly outperforms' (pp. 20, 24); a negative Maratos result about the new method stated plainly (p. 23); ingredient labels typeset beside the pseudocode (pp. 10-13).
limits_future: No line-search convergence proof (p. 15); infeasible-point convergence not analysed (p. 7); needs SOC, watchdog or non-monotone steps for fast local convergence (p. 23); small CUTEst only; only baseline is the authors' own filter and kappa was tuned on the comparison set (p. 19, not stated as a limit by the authors); Uno to be extended to MPECs and robust optimization (p. 2).

quotes.text: We can now interpret the funnel as a filter with a single entry, NF = 1, that corresponds to the upper bound on the constraint violation, and we update this upper bound on h-type iterations.
This demonstrates that the funnel method also suffers from the Maratos effect.
